newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends session slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends session slightly lower.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended its two-hour trading on Tuesday 0.06 percent lower due mainly to a fall in leading Societe Nationale d'Investissment, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 433.95 points from 434.21 points on Monday.
SNI, the country's second largest private conglomerate, lost five dirhams in one session to close at 530 dirhams. The conglomerate has a market capitalisation of more than 5.5 billion dirhams.
"The bourse index change reflected an adjustment of the market activity...It is expected to return soon to its upward trend," a trader said.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private group which holds stakes in more than 100 firms, was not traded. It was exchanged at 490 dirhams per share on Monday.
First tranche of privatisation bonds which were issued in January lost five dirhams to close at 1,140 dirhams while second tranche issued in April, closed at 1,068 dirhams.
The bonds are negotiable on the bourse or can be swapped for equity in future privatisations.
Wafabank, a market blue-chip, dropped to 523 dirhams from 525 dirhams on the previous session.
Morocco's steel mill SONASID fell one dirham to trade at 325 dirhams.
Traded volume was not immediately available.
